mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reflects a broad reopening trend that increases weekday footfall, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -52.7 to -30.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility crosses above -10 percent change, it signals that essential-trip normalization has removed a constraint on discretionary travel, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -21.1 to -9.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If, after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds -10, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of declining RESIDENTIAL mobility and rising PARKS mobility indicates increased out-of-home leisure, which spills over into retail-and-recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 and PARKS rises above -10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.4 to 9.4 while PARKS rose from -37.3 to -6.9
failure_condition: If the joint condition occurs but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Under a loosening-restrictions regime, TRANSIT recovery leads retail recovery because commuting patterns precede shopping trips, so continued TRANSIT gains predict higher RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -54.9 to -41.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If in weeks with a loosening-restrictions regime, TRANSIT gains are not followed by higher RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal transition from winter to early spring increases outdoor activity, as captured by PARKS mobility, and this outdoor activity complements retail-and-recreation trips, driving RETAIL_REC up over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -37.3 to -6.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility rises but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -25 percent change, it signals a policy-driven return to offices that boosts nearby retail footfall, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -30.7 to -23.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If after WORKPLACES exceeds -25, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than over the prior 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: Pandemic fatigue, evident in the four-week decline of RESIDENTIAL mobility, reduces caution and increases discretionary trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.4 to 9.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: If the decline in RESIDENTIAL does not lead to a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT mobility signals broader normalization of daily routines; when both improve together, they amplify retail-and-recreation mobility, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves and TRANSIT improves week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -21.1 to -9.9 and TRANSIT from -54.9 to -41.7
failure_condition: If simultaneous weekly improvements in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT do not precede a higher RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days.
